newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU statistics show beef population up.
newsitem.headline: EU statistics show beef population up.

text.p: The European Union's cattle population increased slightly overall despite the mad cow crisis, a report published on Friday by the European Commission's statistical organisation Eurostat says.
The cattle population survey was carried out between May and June (1996) after the outbreak of Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE).
It showed that the dairy herd continued to shrink slowly and was down by 0.8 percent. The rearing of bull calves was also down by two percent.
These declines were offset by more extensive meat production resulting from greater numbers of suckler cows whose numbers were up by 1.8 per cent.
This meant that in overall terms the cattle population increased by 0.7 percent.

But the mad cow crisis led to a fall in the supply of meat for human consumption which dropped by five per cent compared with the previous year (1995) due to the number of animals being culled, mainly in the United Kingdom.
The report concludes that the results of the survey represent a snapshot view reflecting "momentary effects as much as underlying trends". -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
